title: The hadith of Jibril
hook: Islam, iman, ihsan, and the signs of the Hour, taught in one scene (Muslim)

segments.voice: Yesterday, draw near a span, and your line: he comes running. Did you take the span you chose? Day one thousand one hundred sixty.

Umar ibn al-Khattab tells this one himself. One day, he says, we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, when a man came up to us, his clothes intensely white, his hair intensely black. No mark of travel on him, and not one of us knew him. He sat down close, his knees against the Prophet's knees, his hands on his thighs, and began to ask questions. Long ago on this path we stopped at one of those questions, the one about ihsan. Today we take the whole scene, from the first question to the moment the stranger is named. The hadith of Jibril.
screen: `WHITE CLOTHES, BLACK HAIR.` → `KNEES TO KNEES.` → `THE WHOLE SCENE TODAY.`

segments.voice: First, three questions, in order. What is Islam? The Prophet names the pillars: the testimony, prayer, zakat, the fast of Ramadan, and the pilgrimage for whoever is able. What is iman, faith? To believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, its good and its bad. What is ihsan? To worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, He sees you. After each answer the stranger says: you have spoken truly. Umar says they were amazed, a man who asks and then confirms. Second, the question with no date. When is the Hour, the stranger asks. And the Prophet answers: the one being asked knows no more about it than the one asking. A teacher, in front of his students, saying I don't know, and making it part of the lesson. Third, the signs. Then tell me its signs, the man says. The Prophet names two. That a slave woman will give birth to her mistress. And that you'll see barefoot, unclothed, destitute shepherds competing in building tall buildings. Commentators have read these in more than one way; several readings point to a world turned upside down. Fourth, the reveal. The man leaves. Umar says he stayed a while, and then the Prophet asked him: Umar, do you know who the questioner was? Allah and His Messenger know best, Umar says. It was Jibril, the Prophet tells him. He came to teach you your religion. So in this report the whole religion arrives as questions, asked by someone who already knew the answers, so the people sitting there could hear them.
screen: `ISLAM, IMAN, IHSAN.` · `THE ONE ASKED KNOWS NO MORE.` · `TWO SIGNS OF THE HOUR.` · `HE CAME TO TEACH YOU YOUR RELIGION.`

segments.voice: The practice: reread it. Settle, and breathe. Tell the scene back to yourself slowly, in your own words, one beat for each breath. The stranger in white. Knees to knees. Islam. Iman. Ihsan. When is the Hour? The one asked knows no more. The two signs. Umar, do you know who that was? Then let the scene go quiet, and pick the one of the three questions you'd like to sit with this week: what you do, what you believe, or how you do it. Just choose. If you'd like, later today, find the full report in Sahih Muslim and read it through once. The bell holds the time.
The hadith of Jibril. The angel comes as a stranger and asks about Islam, iman, ihsan and the Hour, to teach the companions their religion. Today's word.

Your line: islam, iman, ihsan. Today, ask one real question of someone who knows more than you, even if you think you know the answer. Tomorrow: women who carried hadith. Day one thousand one hundred sixty.

howItsDone: Muslims study the hadith of Jibril as a summary of the religion, and teachers use it to introduce Islam, iman and ihsan to new students.

what it means: Jibril comes as a stranger and asks the questions that lay out the religion.
what a scholar hears: a lesson taught as questions, with an honest I don't know about the Hour at its center.

notes: Muslim 8 (hadith of Jibril, narrated by Umar): confirm number; the whole scene is paraphrased.
Iman list given as in Muslim 8 (Allah, angels, books, messengers, Last Day, decree good and bad): confirm.

Signs of the Hour: 'a slave woman gives birth to her mistress' and 'barefoot, unclothed, destitute shepherds competing in building': confirm paraphrase. Interpretations are only described as 'more than one way'.
'Umar says he stayed a while': Muslim's wording is often rendered 'I stayed a long while'; confirm.
Day 294 (year 1) covered ihsan from this hadith; this day widens to the whole scene, the Hour and the reveal to avoid repeating that angle.
